items.stem: Why are role-based or test-id locators preferred over selectors tied to CSS class names?

options.text: They are more stable because they do not break when styling or generated class names change
options.rationale: Correct: resilient locators reduce test brittleness.

options.text: They make the page render faster
options.rationale: Locators do not affect rendering speed.

options.text: They remove the need for waits

items.stem: What is the main problem with using fixed sleeps (e.g. sleep 3s) in E2E tests?

options.text: They are either too short (flaky) or too long (slow), unlike condition-based waits
options.rationale: Correct: condition-based waiting is both faster and more reliable.

options.text: They are not supported by any framework

items.explanation: Correct: condition-based waiting is both faster and more reliable.

items.stem: Which statements about the Page Object pattern are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: It centralises selectors and page actions so tests are less brittle
options.rationale: Correct: changes to a page are made in one place.

options.text: It improves reuse by sharing actions like login across tests
options.rationale: Correct: common flows become reusable methods.

options.text: It requires putting raw selectors in every test
options.rationale: False; it removes selectors from tests.

options.text: It eliminates the need for assertions
options.rationale: False; tests still assert on outcomes.

items.explanation: Correct: changes to a page are made in one place.; Correct: common flows become reusable methods.
